title: Proposed service-constraint model
provenance: New qualitative model created at the user's request after the original model was not supplied. Not a reconstruction or an empirical result.
purpose: Generate bounded comparisons and questions about displaced burdens.
limitations: No fitted weights, causal identification, intervention estimates or centrality ranking.
Edge directions are conditional hypotheses; feedback timing is unspecified.
Context sources do not validate an edge or quantify its effect.
The diagram shows candidate relationships, not completeness or global importance.

nodes.label: System energy density
nodes.definition: Usable energy per mass or volume of the installed storage system.
nodes.question: Does storage mass or volume bind in this service?

nodes.label: Useful service per joule
nodes.definition: A service of declared quality from a unit of input energy.
nodes.question: Could efficiency or service redesign remove more of the constraint?

nodes.label: Delivery & infrastructure
nodes.definition: Generation, networks, charging, storage and maintenance.
nodes.question: Is availability constrained by delivery rather than storage?

nodes.label: Cost & access
nodes.definition: Who can afford and obtain the required service.
nodes.question: Which cost or access barrier determines uptake?

nodes.label: Useful services
nodes.definition: Mobility, heat, food production, industrial output and computation.
nodes.question: Which service, beneficiary, quality and duration are held fixed?

nodes.label: Scientific computation
nodes.definition: More task-qualified computational work for research.
nodes.question: Does extra compute produce reproducible useful research?

nodes.label: Aggregate demand
nodes.definition: The total amount of service consumed, not just intensity.
nodes.question: How much growth is caused by lower cost versus other drivers?

nodes.label: Lifecycle burdens
nodes.definition: Materials, water, land, emissions, waste heat and safety.
nodes.question: Which burdens rise, where, when and for whom?

edges.assumption: Mass or volume is a binding constraint; installed-system overhead does not erase the gain.
edges.discriminating_test: Compare delivered service at fixed system mass or volume and duty cycle.

edges.assumption: Changes in materials, manufacturing and lifetime can outweigh storage gains.
edges.discriminating_test: Compare full lifecycle costs at identical service and reliability.

edges.assumption: A denser chemistry or carrier changes extraction, containment and end-of-life burdens.
edges.discriminating_test: Publish a comparative lifecycle inventory with material quantities and uncertainty.

edges.assumption: Operating energy costs matter and savings are not fully offset by capital or maintenance.
edges.discriminating_test: Compare total costs using a declared duty cycle and lifetime.

edges.assumption: The same service is delivered and manufacturing overhead does not erase operating savings.
edges.discriminating_test: Compare whole-system totals across lifecycle and demand scenarios.

edges.assumption: Delivery or availability constrains the service.
edges.discriminating_test: Compare outage, queue or curtailment data before and after an intervention.

edges.assumption: Infrastructure adds embodied impacts but can reduce other losses.
edges.discriminating_test: Include construction, replacement and displaced equipment in the inventory.

edges.assumption: The cost variable is service price and demand responds to it.
edges.discriminating_test: Estimate a price response using a credible counterfactual; separate unrelated growth.

edges.assumption: Marginal service has nonzero resource requirements.
edges.discriminating_test: Measure aggregate consumption and marginal supply effects.

edges.assumption: Energy costs materially constrain research compute and capacity can expand.
edges.discriminating_test: Compare energy share of compute cost and actual capacity constraints.

edges.assumption: Additional research compute may produce valid, deployable improvements.
edges.discriminating_test: Compare independently validated research yield per total resource cost.

edges.assumption: Extra search produces replicable, manufacturable storage improvements.
edges.discriminating_test: Audit discoveries against prior art and independent physical tests.

edges.assumption: Changes in service quality, access and substitution alter total use.
edges.discriminating_test: Track uptake, displaced services, quality and absolute consumption.

sector_questions.climate: Do lifecycle emissions fall in total and per service?
sector_questions.transportation: Does storage mass, volume, power, refuelling, infrastructure or demand bind?
sector_questions.agriculture: Does useful energy constrain food output after water, land and nutrients?
sector_questions.computation: Does energy constrain quality-qualified tasks after hardware and latency?
sector_questions.industrial production: What temperature, uptime and process change is required?
sector_questions.finance: Do capital access or financing terms dominate lifecycle economics?
sector_questions.supply chains: Which materials, manufacturers and transport routes constrain scale?
sector_questions.geopolitics: Does supplier concentration or dependence increase?
sector_questions.infrastructure: What must be built, maintained and replaced, and by when?
